title: Build a todo CLI with subcommands
prompt:
Please implement todo.py, a small todo-list command line tool (python3 standard library only, use argparse). Spec:

    python3 todo.py [--db PATH] <command> ...

--db is the JSON file the tasks are stored in (default: todo.json in the current directory). A missing file just means there are no tasks yet; it's created on the first change. The file layout is up to you, but it must be JSON.

Commands:

- `add TEXT... [--priority low|normal|high]` (default priority normal). The words are joined with single spaces and surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Prints `Added #<id>: <text>`. Ids start at 1 and go up; an id is never reused, even after the task with the highest id is removed.
- `list [--all] [--priority P]` prints pending tasks in id order, one per line, as `#<id> [ ] <text>`. With --all, done tasks are included too, shown as `#<id> [x] <text>`. High-priority tasks get ` (!)` appended. --priority shows only tasks with that priority. If there's nothing to show it prints `No tasks.`
- `done ID [ID ...]` marks tasks done and prints `Done #<id>` for each, in the order given; for a task that was already done it prints `#<id> was already done` instead.
- `remove ID` deletes a task and prints `Removed #<id>: <text>`.

Errors: a problem with the user's data (an id that doesn't exist, empty task text, a --db file that exists but isn't a valid todo database) prints a message starting with `error:` to stderr, prints nothing to stdout, exits with status 1 and changes nothing — e.g. `done 1 7` when #7 doesn't exist must not mark #1 either, and the error should say which id was missing. A broken db file must be left exactly as it was. Invalid usage (unknown command, missing arguments, a non-numeric id, an unknown priority) should get argparse's normal usage error with exit status 2. Successful commands exit 0.
